lit: joy that goes out beyond what one had hoped for

use.how: Predicate about a person, often after 让 or 令: 这个消息让她喜出望外。 The good news or luck must be unexpected.

near.diff: 得意洋洋 is smug pride shown off after one's own success; 喜出望外 is delight at good news one did not expect.

cue: You entered a contest just for fun and forgot all about it. Months later a call tells you that you won first prize. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 本以为没希望了，听说考试通过了，他{喜出望外}。
ctx.en: He had thought there was no hope, so when he heard he had passed the exam he was overjoyed.

ctx.s: 多年没联系的老朋友突然来看我，真让我{喜出望外}。
ctx.en: An old friend I hadn't heard from in years suddenly came to see me. What a wonderful surprise.

ctx.s: 妈妈没想到孩子会记得她的生日，收到礼物时{喜出望外}。
ctx.en: Mum never expected the kids to remember her birthday, and she was overjoyed when the present arrived.

ctx.s: 公司突然给每人发了一笔奖金，大家是不是都{喜出望外}？
ctx.en: The company suddenly gave everyone a bonus. Weren't you all delighted?

ctx.s: 丢了三天的小狗竟然自己找回了家，全家人{喜出望外}。
ctx.en: The puppy that had been lost for three days found its own way home, and the whole family was overjoyed.

ctx.s: 球迷们早已不抱希望，没想到球队在最后一分钟逆转取胜，大家{喜出望外}。
ctx.en: The fans had long given up hope, but the team turned the game around in the last minute and everyone was overjoyed.

bad.s: 我早就知道会升职，所以今天{喜出望外}。
bad.en: (meant: I knew I'd be promoted, so I'm very happy today)
bad.why: The joy must come from something unexpected; if you already knew, it cannot be beyond your hopes. Just say you are very happy.

bad.s: 我每天下班回家都{喜出望外}。
bad.en: (meant: I am happy every day when I get home from work)
bad.why: It is a reaction to one piece of unexpected good news, not an everyday routine happiness. Just say you are happy to get home.

mean: to love something too much to put it down
lit: to love it so much one will not let it go from one's hand

story.text: Xiao Tong, crown prince of the Liang dynasty and compiler of the anthology Wenxuan, also edited the collected works of the poet Tao Yuanming. In his preface he wrote that he loved Tao's writing so much that he could not let it out of his hands, and that he regretted not having lived in the poet's time. His phrase, could not let it out of his hands, is the source of the idiom.
story.source: 南朝梁·萧统《陶渊明集序》

use.how: Predicate or complement about an object one can hold: a book, a toy, a gadget. 对这本书爱不释手、让人爱不释手。

near.diff: 恋恋不舍 is reluctance to leave a person or place; 爱不释手 is about an object held in one's hands.

cue: Your nephew got a toy car for his birthday and carries it everywhere, even to the dinner table and to bed. How would you describe him with it?

ctx.s: 这本漫画书太好看了，我{爱不释手}。
ctx.en: This comic book is so good I can't put it down.

ctx.s: 孩子拿到新玩具，{爱不释手}，连睡觉都抱着。
ctx.en: Once the child got the new toy he wouldn't let go of it, and even slept holding it.

ctx.s: 这只手工杯子做得很精致，让人{爱不释手}。
ctx.en: This handmade cup is so finely made you don't want to put it down.

ctx.s: “你怎么又在看那块表？”“没办法，我对它{爱不释手}。”
ctx.en: "Are you looking at that watch again?" "I can't help it, I just love holding it."

ctx.s: 爷爷对这套旧邮票{爱不释手}，每天都要拿出来看一看。
ctx.en: Grandpa treasures this set of old stamps and takes them out to look at every day.

ctx.s: 这款相机手感极好，不少用户试用后都{爱不释手}。
ctx.en: This camera feels great in the hand; many users didn't want to give it back after trying it.

bad.s: 我对妈妈{爱不释手}。
bad.en: (meant: I love my mother deeply)
bad.why: It is said about objects held in the hand, such as books, toys and gadgets. Said about a person it sounds absurd.

bad.s: 离开家乡的时候，我对那里{爱不释手}。
bad.en: (meant: I hated to leave my hometown)
bad.why: A place cannot be held in the hand. Reluctance to leave a place or person is liàn liàn bù shě.

use.how: Attributive, predicate or adverbial about a person's whole state of mind or way of life: 无忧无虑的童年、过得无忧无虑。

near.diff: 自由自在 is being free of restraint, doing as one likes; 无忧无虑 is having nothing on one's mind to worry about.

cue: You remember the summers you spent as a small child on your grandparents' farm, long before exams, rent or bills. What were those days like?

ctx.s: 孩子们不知道家里遇到了困难，还在{无忧无虑}地玩耍。
ctx.en: The children don't know the family is in trouble and are still playing without a care in the world.

ctx.s: 我真怀念那段{无忧无虑}的童年。
ctx.en: I really miss that carefree childhood.

ctx.s: 退休以后，他不用再为工作操心，过得{无忧无虑}。
ctx.en: Since retiring he no longer has to fret about work, and he lives without a worry.

ctx.s: 不用为钱发愁，也不用为孩子操心，谁不想过{无忧无虑}的日子呢？
ctx.en: No fretting about money, no worrying about the kids: who wouldn't want a life without worries?

ctx.s: 看着那些{无忧无虑}的新生，我想起了刚入学的自己。
ctx.en: Watching those carefree freshmen, I remembered myself when I first started university.

ctx.s: 父母什么都替她安排好了，她从小就生活得{无忧无虑}。
ctx.en: Her parents arranged everything for her, so she grew up without a care.

bad.s: 他对考试结果{无忧无虑}。
bad.en: (meant: he isn't worried about the exam result)
bad.why: It describes a whole carefree mood or life, not lack of worry about one particular thing. Simply say he is not worried about the result.

bad.s: 他做事{无忧无虑}，经常忘记锁门。
bad.en: (meant: he is careless and often forgets to lock the door)
bad.why: It is a happy freedom from worry, not carelessness. For careless habits say cū xīn dà yì.

lit: free in oneself, at ease in oneself

use.how: Adverbial or predicate about people or animals not held back by rules or others: 自由自在地游、过得自由自在。

near.diff: 无忧无虑 is having no worries on one's mind; 自由自在 is being free to move and act as one likes.

cue: A bird that lived for years in a small cage is released and flies wherever it likes over the open fields. How is it flying?

ctx.s: 鱼儿在河里{自由自在}地游来游去。
ctx.en: The fish swim freely back and forth in the river.

ctx.s: 放暑假了，我终于可以{自由自在}地睡懒觉了。
ctx.en: Summer holidays have started, and at last I can sleep in as long as I like.

ctx.s: 他一个人住，想几点回家就几点回家，过得{自由自在}。
ctx.en: He lives alone and comes home whenever he likes; his life is free and easy.

ctx.s: 在大城市上班虽然挣得多，哪有在老家{自由自在}？
ctx.en: You may earn more working in a big city, but how could it be as free and easy as back home?

ctx.s: 离开了管得很严的父母，她第一次感到{自由自在}。
ctx.en: Away from her strict parents, she felt free for the first time.

ctx.s: 草原上没有围栏，马群{自由自在}地奔跑。
ctx.en: There are no fences on the grassland, and the horses gallop wherever they please.

bad.s: 他说话太{自由自在}，经常得罪人。
bad.en: (meant: he speaks too bluntly and often offends people)
bad.why: It is a pleasant feeling of being unconstrained, not a criticism of unruly speech. Say he speaks too carelessly.

bad.s: 这次考试{自由自在}，没有固定题目。
bad.en: (meant: this exam is open, with no fixed questions)
bad.why: It describes a person or animal free to act as it likes, not the format of an event. Say the format of the exam is open.

lit: so pleased with oneself that it overflows

story.text: Yan Ying was chief minister of the state of Qi. His charioteer's wife watched through the gate as her husband drove him past: under the great canopy, whipping the four horses, the driver looked thoroughly pleased with himself. When he came home she asked to leave him. Yan Ying, she said, is minister of Qi and famous among the states, yet he is humble; you are only a driver and you look so satisfied with yourself. After that the driver restrained himself, and when Yan Ying learned why, he recommended him for office.

use.how: Usually adverbial before a verb, or 得意洋洋的样子. Describes visible smugness after a success, with mild disapproval or teasing: 他得意洋洋地说。

near.diff: 喜出望外 is delight at good news one did not expect; 得意洋洋 is showing off one's own success.

cue: Your little brother beats you at chess for the first time and struts around the house telling everyone about it. How is he acting?

ctx.s: 弟弟下棋赢了我，{得意洋洋}地跑去告诉妈妈。
ctx.en: My little brother beat me at chess and ran off to tell Mum, looking very pleased with himself.

ctx.s: 他刚买了新车，{得意洋洋}地开到公司给大家看。
ctx.en: He had just bought a new car and drove it to the office to show everyone, smug as anything.

ctx.s: 看你那{得意洋洋}的样子，是不是又考了满分？
ctx.en: Look how pleased with yourself you are. Did you get full marks again?

ctx.s: 比赛还没结束呢，先别{得意洋洋}。
ctx.en: The match isn't over yet, so don't get smug.

ctx.s: 小猫抓到一只老鼠，{得意洋洋}地叼到主人面前。
ctx.en: The kitten caught a mouse and proudly carried it in its mouth to its owner.

ctx.s: 骗子以为没人发现，正{得意洋洋}，警察就敲门了。
ctx.en: The con man thought no one had noticed and was feeling very pleased with himself when the police knocked at the door.

bad.s: 听说奶奶的病好了，全家人都{得意洋洋}。
bad.en: (meant: the family was overjoyed that Grandma had recovered)
bad.why: It is smugness about one's own success. Joy at good news about someone else is xǐ chū wàng wài, or simply being very happy.

bad.s: 他很谦虚，拿了奖也只是{得意洋洋}地笑了笑。
bad.en: (meant: he is modest; when he won he just smiled contentedly)
bad.why: It means visible smugness, the opposite of modesty. A modest person just smiles happily.

mean: living in constant fear and worry
lit: to lift up one's heart and hang up one's gallbladder (the seat of courage)

use.how: Predicate or adverbial for fear that lasts while one waits for something bad: 整天提心吊胆、提心吊胆地过日子。 Not for a sudden fright.

near.diff: 胆战心惊 is intense, trembling terror; 提心吊胆 is anxious fear dragging on while one waits for something bad to happen.

cue: Your teenage son is travelling alone across the country for the first time, and until he calls you keep imagining accidents. How do you spend those days?

ctx.s: 孩子第一次一个人出远门，妈妈整天{提心吊胆}。
ctx.en: Her child is travelling far alone for the first time, and the mother is on edge all day long.

ctx.s: 走在结了冰的路上，我{提心吊胆}，生怕摔倒。
ctx.en: Walking on the icy road, I was on tenterhooks, afraid of falling.

ctx.s: 公司要裁员的消息传开后，大家都{提心吊胆}地上班。
ctx.en: After news of layoffs spread, everyone went to work in constant fear.

ctx.s: 你天天这样{提心吊胆}的，不累吗？
ctx.en: Living in fear like this every day, aren't you exhausted?

ctx.s: 那座旧桥摇摇晃晃，我们{提心吊胆}地走了过去。
ctx.en: The old bridge swayed, and we crossed it with our hearts in our mouths.

ctx.s: 他借了高利贷，从那以后过着{提心吊胆}的日子。
ctx.en: He borrowed from loan sharks, and from then on he lived in constant fear.

bad.s: 突然一声巨响，他{提心吊胆}地跳了起来。
bad.en: (meant: there was a sudden bang and he jumped up in fright)
bad.why: It is drawn-out anxiety, not a sudden scare. For a sudden fright say xià le yí tiào.

bad.s: 我对明天的旅行很{提心吊胆}，太期待了。
bad.en: (meant: I'm so excited about tomorrow's trip)
bad.why: It means fear and dread, not excitement. Say you are looking forward to it or excited.

mean: at a loss for what to do
lit: not knowing where to place oneself (cuò: to put, to arrange)

use.how: Predicate or complement, often with 一时 or after 得: 一时不知所措、紧张得不知所措。 A flustered moment when something sudden happens.

near.diff: 左右为难 is having two options and finding both costly; 不知所措 is being flustered with no idea at all how to react.

cue: On the subway a stranger suddenly bursts into tears right in front of you, and you just stand there frozen, hands hanging. How do you react?

ctx.s: 第一次上台演讲，我紧张得{不知所措}。
ctx.en: The first time I gave a speech on stage I was so nervous I didn't know what to do with myself.

ctx.s: 面对突然的表白，她一时{不知所措}，脸都红了。
ctx.en: Faced with a sudden declaration of love, she was flustered for a moment and blushed.

ctx.s: 电脑突然黑屏，刚学电脑的奶奶{不知所措}。
ctx.en: The screen suddenly went black, and Grandma, who had only just learned to use a computer, was at a loss.

ctx.s: 要是在国外丢了护照，你会不会{不知所措}？
ctx.en: If you lost your passport abroad, would you know what to do?

ctx.s: 孩子在超市里找不到妈妈，站在那儿{不知所措}。
ctx.en: The child couldn't find his mother in the supermarket and just stood there, lost.

ctx.s: 这个意外的问题让发言人{不知所措}，会场安静了好几秒。
ctx.en: The unexpected question left the spokesperson at a loss, and the hall went silent for several seconds.

bad.s: 选专业时，我在中文和法律之间{不知所措}。
bad.en: (meant: I was torn between Chinese and law)
bad.why: Being torn between two specific choices is zuǒ yòu wéi nán; this idiom is flustered confusion with no idea what to do.

bad.s: 他是个{不知所措}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is an indecisive person)
bad.why: It describes a momentary reaction to a sudden situation, not a personality trait. Say he is indecisive.

lit: difficult on the left, difficult on the right

use.how: Predicate, often after 让, 使 or 感到: 这件事让我左右为难。 Said when two people, sides or choices pull against each other.

near.diff: 不知所措 is flustered confusion with no idea what to do; 左右为难 means the options are clear but each one costs something.

cue: Your mother and your wife each want you to spend the holiday with them, in different cities, and whichever you choose, the other will be hurt.

ctx.s: 两个好朋友同一天办婚礼，去了这边就去不了那边，真是{左右为难}。
ctx.en: Two good friends are holding their weddings on the same day; if I go to one I can't go to the other. I'm really torn.

ctx.s: 妈妈和妻子意见不同，他夹在中间{左右为难}。
ctx.en: His mother and his wife disagree, and he is caught in the middle.

ctx.s: 一边是高薪的工作，一边是生病的父亲，这让她{左右为难}。
ctx.en: On one side a well-paid job, on the other her sick father: she is torn.

ctx.s: 客户要快，老板要省钱，你说我是不是{左右为难}？
ctx.en: The client wants it fast and the boss wants it cheap. Tell me, am I not stuck in the middle?

ctx.s: 这套房离公司近，那套离学校近，我们{左右为难}了很久。
ctx.en: This flat is close to work, that one close to the school; we went back and forth for ages.

ctx.s: 两位老师都请他当助手，他谁也不想得罪，感到{左右为难}。
ctx.en: Both teachers asked him to be their assistant; he didn't want to offend either and felt torn.

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我{左右为难}。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is too hard for me)
bad.why: There must be two competing choices or sides. For a problem you can't solve, just say you can't work it out.

bad.s: 我{左右为难}地选了红色。
bad.en: (meant: after hesitating, I chose red)
bad.why: It describes the dilemma itself, not the manner of an action. Say you hesitated for a long time before choosing red.

mean: powerless to do anything about it
lit: having no ability to put one's strength to use

use.how: Predicate, often 对……无能为力 or 我也无能为力. States that something is beyond one's power, usually when one would like to help.

near.diff: 无可奈何 stresses the sighing feeling of having to accept something; 无能为力 states plainly that one lacks the power to act.

cue: A friend begs you to get her son a job at your company, but hiring is decided at head office and you have no say at all. What do you tell her?

ctx.s: 对不起，这件事我真的{无能为力}。
ctx.en: I'm sorry, there's really nothing I can do about this.

ctx.s: 医生说病情太严重了，他们也{无能为力}。
ctx.en: The doctors said the illness was too advanced and there was nothing more they could do.

ctx.s: 手机掉进了深海，就算是最好的维修师傅也{无能为力}。
ctx.en: The phone fell into the deep sea; even the best repairman couldn't do anything about it.

ctx.s: 难道我们对这种浪费就{无能为力}吗？
ctx.en: Are we really powerless to stop this kind of waste?

ctx.s: “能帮我把成绩改一下吗？”“成绩已经交上去了，我也{无能为力}。”
ctx.en: "Could you change my grade?" "The grades have already been submitted. It's out of my hands."

ctx.s: 他很想帮那位老人，可自己身无分文，实在{无能为力}。
ctx.en: He badly wanted to help the old man, but he didn't have a penny on him and could do nothing.

bad.s: 他太懒了，对工作{无能为力}。
bad.en: (meant: he's too lazy to do any work)
bad.why: It means unable despite wanting to, not unwilling. For laziness, say he is unwilling to do anything.

bad.s: 我今天很累，{无能为力}去跑步了。
bad.en: (meant: I'm too tired to go running today)
bad.why: It is not a modal placed before a verb, and it is about things beyond one's power to change. Say you have no energy to go running.

mean: resigned, with no other way out
lit: there is nothing at all that can be done about it (nài hé: what can be done)

use.how: Adverbial (无可奈何地+verb), attributive (无可奈何的笑) or predicate (对……无可奈何). Conveys reluctant, sighing acceptance.

near.diff: 无能为力 states that one lacks the power to act; 无可奈何 stresses the resigned feeling of accepting what one cannot change.

cue: Rain cancels the picnic you planned for weeks. You shrug, sigh and slowly unpack the basket on the kitchen table. How do you unpack it?

ctx.s: 下雨了，野餐只好取消，孩子们{无可奈何}地回了家。
ctx.en: It rained and the picnic had to be called off, so the children reluctantly went home.

ctx.s: 他摇摇头，露出{无可奈何}的笑容。
ctx.en: He shook his head with a resigned smile.

ctx.s: 儿子不听劝，父母对他也{无可奈何}。
ctx.en: Their son won't listen to advice, and his parents can only throw up their hands.

ctx.s: 末班车已经开走了，他{无可奈何}地叫了一辆出租车。
ctx.en: The last bus had already left, so with a sigh he called a taxi.

ctx.s: 看着心爱的花一朵朵凋谢，她感到{无可奈何}。
ctx.en: Watching her beloved flowers wilt one by one, she felt there was nothing to be done.

ctx.s: 弟弟一直缠着我讲故事，我{无可奈何}，只好又讲了一个。
ctx.en: My little brother kept pestering me for a story, so I gave in and told him another one.

bad.s: 这台机器{无可奈何}，修不好了。
bad.en: (meant: this machine can't be repaired)
bad.why: It describes a person's resigned feeling, not the state of a thing. A machine feels nothing; it is the people who must accept it.

bad.s: 他{无可奈何}地拿下了冠军。
bad.en: (meant: no one could stop him from winning the title)
bad.why: It expresses the subject's own reluctant resignation, not that others could not stop him. Say he was unstoppable (shì bù kě dǎng).
